stills.prompt: A real night-time boutique corner: warm neon tubes spelling the offer glow on a dark plaster or brick wall, the bag standing on a stool or plinth below the sign, lit by its own soft white spotlight so its true colour reads clearly (the neon only rims it), a little haze, shot on a phone, real reflections, nothing CGI; the story line is set small in clean white print type on the wall below the sign, not in neon. The black hobo bag closed on a wooden bench in a quiet tiled station at night, a warm red neon sign glowing on the wall above, soft white light on the bag. The exact handbag from the reference image, unchanged: same colour (galaxy black), same shape and proportions, same handles or straps, same zipper pulls and hardware, same stitching and finish. Do not redesign it. The handbag is closed and zipped; its inside is never shown. The only words in the image, each exactly once and spelled exactly as written: "50% OFF" / "Late train home. Cards on your side.". Set them as neon tube lettering, warm pink-red or white glow, perfectly spelled, big, sharp and easy to read on a small phone screen (the main line spans most of the picture's width), never over the handbag. No other text anywhere: no logos, no brand names, no labels or writing on the handbag, no watermark. The offer "50% OFF" is the boldest, largest wording in the picture, read in under a second, with perfectly drawn numerals and percent sign. The line "Late train home. Cards on your side." is the second voice of the ad: smaller than the offer but clearly readable on a phone, never tiny or faint; the picture shows the moment it tells. Nobody is in the picture, not even blurred in the background. Every photographic part looks like a real photograph: true-to-life light and colour, real textures and materials, small natural imperfections, nothing glossy, plastic or computer-generated. Portrait 4:5 composition, the handbag large and clearly visible.

steps: 1. Upload each distinct `ref` once (media_upload, curl PUT, media_confirm); generate every still with generate_image_batch (model/params/prompt as listed, medias [{value: media_id, role: image_references}], max 12 per call); jobs_wait; download each result to $OUT/<file>.

2. python3 pipeline/ai_gen.py gate --out $OUT ; LOOK at $OUT/qa/ai_stills.jpg (reference | still): reject any still where the bag's shape, colour, handles or hardware differ from the reference, or that looks AI: python3 pipeline/ai_gen.py reject --out $OUT AS03 ...

3. For every clip whose start still passed: generate_video_batch (start_image = that still's job id, model/params/prompt as listed); jobs_wait; download to $OUT/<file>. Clips of a rejected still are skipped. If a submission comes back with a preset recommendation instead of a job, send it again with `declined_preset_id` = that preset's id (the project never uses presets).

3b. Motion stills (AM.. clips, `use: motion`): generate_video_batch with medias [{value: <the still's job id>, role: start_image}, {value: <the same job id>, role: end_image}] (the same still first and last, so the loop has no seam), model/params/prompt as listed.

4. python3 pipeline/ai_gen.py clips --out $OUT ; LOOK at $OUT/qa/ai_clips.jpg; reject morphing / odd-hand clips with `reject` (a motion still where the bag changes shape, opens, or anything morphs: `reject AM02`). Then render as usual (it applies the result; a motion still whose clip failed ships as the still static alone).
Report: credits before -> after (balance), how many AI assets passed. Never ship a still or clip you would not believe is real.
